The measurements are right, but calling this major overstates it.

What checks out on page-06.png:
- 6.2 runs x207-1630, 6.3 x414-1422 and 6.4 x261-1575, while 6.1 and 6.5 run x148-1688. So three stacked panels step in and out, and 6.3 is only 65% of the art width.
- The gutters are 53 px (about 4.5 mm), 7, 6 and 23 px.
- 6.1 starts at y405.
- At 1:1 there is a 3 px white line (y2167-2169, about 0.25 mm) inside the top frame of 6.5. That puts a double rule on one edge only. There is also a 1 px light line at y2138 at the bottom of 6.4.
- None of this is too slight to see at print size.

Why it is not major:
- The "page-1 flush grid standard" is not the chapter's standard. The compositor (pipeline/compositor.py fit_clip_contain) deliberately fits each image inside its slot and centres it ("contain_visible_viewport_centered_inside_planned_slot").
- Centred, inset panels appear on pages 2 (2.4), 3 (3.2), 4 (4.3), 5 (5.2), 7 (7.3, 7.5) and 8 (8.3, 8.5).
- Gutters vary chapter-wide (page 3: 12/6/55/55 px). Page 9's first panel starts even lower, at y423.
- The same white hairline double-rule shows up on pages 2, 3, 7 and 8, for example 7.2 bottom at y1222-1224.
- Page 6 is the most pronounced case, not a one-off defect. Nothing is hidden or cropped, all lettering reads, speaker order is clear, and the script's one layout requirement ("6.5 Full width, bottom") is met.
- 6.5 lands cleanly as a full-width, text-free panel. The 23 px gap above it actually separates it from 6.4.

Conclusion: this is a real layout-polish issue. Worth fixing:
- Even out the gutters.
- Re-crop 6.2-6.4 toward the full width, or at least make the insets match.
- Strip the baked-in white rule from the top of 6.5.

It is not a localized error of major severity.

confirmed.description: The walk's final beat tells a different story. Nagoji is alone at the doorway, leaning in with one hand on the frame as if he found the room himself. Duarte and João (and the guards) have vanished, although 4.2 has them escorting him. The script also asks for his face in profile lit by the glow, but this is a wide shot where his face is a tiny element, and it opens onto an exterior arch with a palm tree and a fort.
confirmed.evidence: Crop of the right third of 4.4: a solitary barefoot Nagoji with his hand on the jamb of a bright red doorway, and no other figure anywhere in the corridor. The left background shows an open archway to a night sky with a palm and a tower.

verdict.reason:
I'm confirming this one. The page 4 crops back up the main part of the claim.

**Panel 4.4: the escorts are gone and Nagoji acts on his own.** He is the only person in the panel. The corridor behind him runs empty all the way back to the arch, so Duarte, João and the guards are not simply cropped out. His pose makes it worse: he leans into the red doorway with his right hand flat on the jamb, as if he were exploring. In 4.2 he is under escort.

**Panel 4.2 against 4.4: his wrists.** The reviewer did not raise this, and it strengthens the claim. In 4.2 his bandaged wrists are chained together in front of his belly. In 4.4 his hands are free and apart, one on the door frame and one at his side. Only the ankle shackle and its trailing chain remain. The next page (5.3) has him tied to the stool, so a moment of apparent freedom here breaks the sense that he is a captive being led.

**Where the claim is weaker.**
- The script's profile-lit-by-glow beat is roughly there. His face is in profile and lit red by the doorway, though it is small in a wide shot.
- The open arch with a palm and fort tower is odd for a dungeon corridor. Panel 4.3 already shows a similar exterior arch, so that part is minor.

**Severity: major, not blocker.** The beat itself survives: the doorway, the red glow, the room kept hidden and the caption are all there. The problem is confined to this one panel. The fix is to redraw 4.4 with at least João behind him or a guard's hand on him, his wrists still chained, and a tighter framing of his profile.

confirmed.description: The reveal room is sunlit and airy, not a sound-swallowing dungeon chamber. Daylight shafts pour through a large arched window onto pale, clean stone, which contradicts the script's mood and the established time of day. Page 1.5 has the evening bells, and 4.3 and 4.4 show a night sky outside. Page 5.2's window then shows dusk. The daylight shafts come back on the floor in 5.3, through the windows in 6.4 and 7.2, and in the bright chapel-like 8.3.

verdict.reason: I confirmed this from crops. On page 5, panel 5.1 (the two-thirds-page reveal), a large barred arched window at upper right throws strong white daylight onto pale, clean flagstones. The window bars cast crisp grid shadows across the floor, and the vault is evenly lit and airy. The brazier is only a small warm accent. The chamber reads as a sunlit hall, not a sealed dungeon room with "vaulted stone thick enough to swallow sound". The chapter itself sets the time as night. Page 1, panel 1.5 has the evening-prayer bells, and panels 4.3 and 4.4 show a dark blue night sky through the corridor arches. Panel 4.4's red glow promises a dark room lit by fire. The same page contradicts itself: panel 5.2's barred window shows a blue dusk townscape with palms, lit windows and a domed church, while panel 5.3 again puts bright sun-shaft grids on the floor under a daylit window. The daylight comes back in 6.1 (cool daylight window), 6.3 and 6.4 (visible light shafts through a window), 7.2 (bright windows behind João and Duarte) and 8.3 (a pale, chapel-like room with a sun shaft on the floor). Neither the script nor CONTINUITY.md allows daylight in the interrogation room. All the script's beats are still present (ropes on an iron ring, brazier, tool table, stool), so this is a lighting and time-of-day continuity error rather than a missing beat. It is major, not blocker: it touches several panels, but the fix is a relight or window removal in 5.1 and 5.3 (plus the small window views in 5.2, 6.x, 7.2 and 8.3). confirmed.description: The interrogation chamber changes from panel to panel, so the scene no longer reads as one room. 6.1 puts Duarte in a sacristy or study (a writing desk with a quill, bookshelves, an altar table crowded with crucifixes, a painted palm mural) apart from Nagoji. 6.2 is a long arcaded hall with braziers on stands. 6.4 has a daylit stair and a different table. 7.1 is a cell with a barred gate. 8.3 is a pale chapel-like vault with a large crucifix and a red-cross banner. confirmed.evidence: 6.1 background: desk with quill and inkwell, a row of standing crosses on an altar-like table, a bookcase at left. 6.2: repeating arcade with three tripod braziers. 8.3: crucifix on the left wall and a black banner with a red cross over the tool table.

verdict.reason:

Page 6 breaks from that room immediately:
- 6.1 (crop checked) shows Duarte in what reads as a study or sacristy. At left are a bookshelf and a desk with a quill, inkwell, candle and books. Behind him is a chest shaped like an altar, holding four or five standing crucifixes. There is a mural painted with palms and a big barred double door. The panel has no ring, no ropes and no tool table.
- 6.2 is a long arcaded hall with three tripod braziers on stands and wall rings.
- 6.4 adds a daylit stone stair at left and a different small table.

The later pages drift too:

- 8.3 does have rib vaults, but it adds a wall crucifix with a candle stand and a black banner with a red cross over a table set against the wall, and it shows no ceiling ring or ropes.

Nothing in the script or the continuity bible allows the setting to change. The script keeps the whole interrogation on pages 5 to 8 in one chamber. 8.3 is explicitly the high shot of 'the stool, the men around it, the brazier', and 8.4 is the ceiling ring.

minors.description: The display chapter title 'Dungeons of Goa' is repeated full-size above the art on every page, not just the opener. The script does not call for it, and it reads as a new chapter title on each page, including the page 5 reveal.
